research_question: Among participants with uremic pruritus, what is the effect of any kappa-opioid agonist (including difelikefalin, nalbuphine, or nalfurafine), compared with placebo, on pruritus severity measured on a 0–10 cm visual analogue scale in parallel-group studies, pooling all eligible agonists as one drug class?
treatment_label: Kappa-opioid agonist therapy (all eligible drugs pooled as one class)
outcome_description: Pruritus severity measured on a 0–10 cm VAS in participants with uremic pruritus. Extract post-treatment means and SDs, or change-from-baseline means and SDs when appropriate and consistently poolable; harmonize any equivalent VAS units to 0–10 cm. Lower raw scores indicate less severe pruritus and a better outcome.
positive_direction: A positive effect means that kappa-opioid agonist treatment produces lower pruritus severity than placebo (i.e., favors the kappa-opioid agonist class).
search_queries: uremic pruritus kappa opioid agonist placebo trial
difelikefalin nalbuphine nalfurafine pruritus controlled study
hemodialysis pruritus kappa agonist placebo quantitative outcome
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies enrolling participants with uremic or chronic kidney disease–associated pruritus.
Parallel-group studies comparing a kappa-opioid agonist, including difelikefalin, nalbuphine, nalfurafine, or another drug in this class, with placebo.
Studies reporting quantitative pruritus severity data measured on a 0–10 cm VAS, or an exactly convertible equivalent, sufficient or potentially sufficient for effect-size calculation.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers.
No eligible parallel-group comparison between a kappa-opioid agonist treatment and placebo; crossover-design studies are excluded as a separate analysis in the review.

No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as means with SDs, convertible t/F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios, including data unobtainable after reasonable author contact.
Completely unrelated to kappa-opioid agonist treatment, uremic pruritus, or the specified pruritus-severity outcome.
moderators_to_extract: Participant kidney-disease context, including hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, or nondialysis CKD
Study design characteristics, including randomization and blinding
effect_size_note: Pool all eligible kappa-opioid agonists together as one class using a mean difference on the common 0–10 cm VAS. Harmonize scales to 0–10 cm before pooling. Orient effects so values favoring treatment correspond to lower pruritus severity. Use an appropriate random-effects model for the primary analysis; do not perform or include the fixed-effect sensitivity analysis requested to remain separate. Do not pool crossover studies in this analysis. Avoid double-counting participants when studies report multiple doses, time points, or publications by combining eligible treatment arms or selecting the prespecified primary/relevant assessment according to a documented hierarchy.
